classes.gamePage: pushed page with back button; install bar pinned above tabs

classes.how: UiMode::Deck; forces wide width class and Density::Controller

density.rule: density follows input device, independent of width (a 1280x800 handheld = wide + touch)

responsive.strategy: key off the root container width via on_sized with an epsilon guard (peek + abs diff > 1.0), not the OS
responsive.deck: Deck is a mode, not a breakpoint: it ignores width classes and scales by safe-zone margins and a user UI scale (1.0 / 1.25 / 1.5 for TV). Pointer and touch still work; they just do not drive focus.

freya.note: Pinned exactly; newest on crates.io, no final 0.5.0 yet. Verified by compiling and rendering headless snapshots in reclaw-ui/.

decisions.decision: One component tree. Input mode is an axis (Density::Controller beside Pointer and Touch) plus a small set of deck-only components. No parallel 'deck' copy of every component.
decisions.why: Two trees drift. Shared components read density; only shelves, glyph hints, slide-in panels and the Play/Stop pair are new.
rejected: a third color theme for deck

decisions.decision: Deck mode is dark only (deck-bg). Daylight is not offered.
decisions.why: TV and handheld OLED viewing; halves the contrast matrix. Deck tokens carry the same value in both themes so lookups never fail.

decisions.decision: Layout class (width) and input density are independent. Deck mode forces the wide layout class and Density::Controller.
decisions.why: A 1280x800 handheld and a 4K TV are both 'wide' but need 56-64px targets.

decisions.decision: The gamepad has one owner at a time: Launcher or App. While an app runs in front, the launcher ignores everything except Guide.
decisions.why: Gamepad readers see every event whatever has window focus; without arbitration the launcher navigates its own menus while the user plays.

decisions.decision: Do not rebuild Steam's overlay or Steam Input. Reclaw owns Guide only when it is the shell; under Steam the Guide binding is removed.
decisions.why: Steam's overlay and mapping already exist in Gaming Mode; two overlays on one button is worse than none.

decisions.decision: Hint glyphs follow the last-used device (gamepad kind, or keyboard keycaps). Face-button labels follow the cap (Nintendo A is East), actions follow position (Confirm is South unless swapped).
decisions.why: Steam does this; showing 'A' to a PlayStation player is wrong.

decisions.decision: Focus targets are declared rectangles computed from layout constants, not measured from the rendered tree. A pure function picks the next target.
decisions.why: Deterministic and unit-testable without a window; the same constants drive scroll offsets so the two cannot disagree.

decisions.decision: Hover never moves focus in Deck mode. Click = focus + confirm. The focus ring is visible only after gamepad or keyboard input.
decisions.why: A resting mouse must not fight the gamepad; Steam hides the ring on mouse use.

decisions.decision: Tile titles are always visible; project, status badge and glow appear on focus, in space reserved up front.
decisions.why: Placeholder art has no baked-in title, and reserved space avoids reflow on every focus move.

decisions.decision: Main menu (left) and Quick Access (right) slide over the page, trap focus, and close with Back. They never shift the layout beneath.
decisions.why: Matches the Big Picture model and keeps the page's focus position intact.

decisions.decision: Stop sends a graceful quit; pressing it again while Stopping force-kills. Apps run in their own process group so the whole tree stops.
decisions.why: Handhelds have no task manager; a hung game must be recoverable from the pad.

decisions.decision: Desktop swaps Play for Stop. Deck shows Resume + Stop side by side while an app runs.
decisions.why: In a controller UI, Resume (A) is what you want 95% of the time, and Stop must not be one mis-press away.

decisions.decision: Per-app controller setup is handed over as SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG plus SDL_JOYSTICK_ALLOW_BACKGROUND_EVENTS. Apps that do not read SDL need a virtual-device layer, which is not built.
decisions.why: Most recompiled-game ports use SDL; this is the one mechanism that needs no kernel permissions.

decisions.decision: Deck mode needs an in-app, gamepad-navigable file browser for 'your game file'. A native dialog cannot be driven by a pad.
decisions.why: The install flow requires the user to choose their own file.

decisions.decision: Deck mode text entry uses an on-screen keyboard opened by Confirm on a field. Specified, not built.
decisions.why: Every search and path field otherwise strands a gamepad user.

detect.unverified: The Steam and gamescope variables are the commonly documented ones; not confirmed on real SteamOS hardware. RECLAW_MODE exists to override a wrong guess.

states.enter: app not running, or ended cleanly
UI sets optimistically on press; cleared by the Started event (spawn is synchronous so it is brief)
Stop pressed; graceful quit sent to the whole process group
ended with a non-zero code or a foreign signal; cleared on next launch

outcomes.ui: Failed: 'Exited with code n', button Retry, log link. Many games exit non-zero on a normal quit, so this is a notice, not 'crashed'.
Failed: 'Closed unexpectedly (signal sig)', button Retry, log link

stop.first: SIGTERM to the process group (Windows: taskkill /T)
stop.grace: 5s default; then SIGKILL to the group
stop.second: pressing Stop while Stopping force-kills immediately
stop.pidReuseGuard: the exit flag is set before events are sent, so the watchdog never signals a reaped pid (a microsecond window remains)

lifecycle.oneSession: start() refuses a second launch of the same app (AlreadyRunning); the table is held across spawn so two quick presses cannot launch two copies
lifecycle.logs: LaunchSpec.log appends stdout and stderr to a file; shown from the Failed state

inputOwnership.onLaunch: launcher goes to the background; owner = App
inputOwnership.onGuide: launcher comes to front, MainMenu opens, owner = Launcher
inputOwnership.onResume: launcher goes to the back, owner = App
inputOwnership.onAppEnded: launcher to front, owner = Launcher; a Failed outcome shows a toast on the game's tile and page
inputOwnership.windowing: bringing windows forward is platform glue (not built); the model emits Effects and tracks inFront

LaunchButton.desktop: Stop (danger variant, square icon) replaces Play
LaunchButton.deck: Resume (install variant) + Stop (danger) side by side

ui.badge: Running (ok tone, play icon) takes priority over Installed on tiles and the hero
ui.NowPlayingBanner: shown at the top of Deck Home while an app is active

platforms.escapes: an app that calls setsid or double-forks leaves the group and is not stopped

verification.workspace: reclaw-input (26 tests), reclaw-runtime (14), reclaw-ui (25 unit, 5 deck snapshots incl. a keyboard-driven reducer test, 3 desktop snapshots, 3 token drift tests, 1 end-to-end lifecycle test)
verification.endToEnd: tests/deck_lifecycle.rs drives the real DeckApp with key presses against a real process: Play launches it and hands the pad to the app (InputOwner(App)); Guide brings the launcher forward (BringLauncherToFront, InputOwner(Launcher)); Back sends it back; Stop ends the process group; the app ending brings the launcher forward again.
verification.driftGuard: tests/tokens_in_sync.rs fails if any color token (both themes), spacing, radius, layout or deck type size in tokens.json differs from the Rust constants.
verification.lint: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features reclaw-ui/gamepad -- -D warnings is clean
notVerified: gilrs backend against real hardware (no /dev/input in the dev container)
Steam and gamescope environment variables on SteamOS
SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG against a real SDL game
visual check beyond headless Skia snapshots on a TV or handheld
